node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Perimeter is boundary length
node.description: Perimeter measures the total length around the outside boundary of a shape.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Area measures surface coverage
node.description: Area measures how much flat surface is covered by a region.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Square units are two dimensional
node.description: Square units measure area because they cover two-dimensional regions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rectangle area uses rows and columns
node.description: Rectangle area can be understood as rows of equal square units times columns of equal square units.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Triangle area is half related rectangle
node.description: A triangle with the same base and height as a related rectangle has half the rectangle's area.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Composite area combines parts
node.description: Composite area can be found by adding or subtracting areas of simpler parts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Radius is half diameter
node.description: The radius of a circle is half its diameter, and the diameter is twice its radius.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Circumference uses pi and diameter
node.description: A circle's circumference is pi times its diameter, or two pi times its radius.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Circle area uses radius squared
node.description: Circle area depends on the square of the radius, not the diameter alone.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Length and area units differ
node.description: Perimeter uses linear units, while area uses square units.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Perimeter area confusion
node.description: Learner confuses boundary length with surface coverage and uses perimeter and area methods interchangeably.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Count grid lines not squares
node.description: Learner counts grid lines or boundary marks instead of square units when finding area.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Double count shared sides
node.description: Learner includes internal shared sides when finding the outside perimeter of composite figures.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Use diameter as radius
node.description: Learner substitutes diameter where radius is required in circle formulas.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Area units written as linear units
node.description: Learner reports area using linear units rather than square units.

edge.rationale: Understanding perimeter as boundary length is foundational to perimeter work.
Measuring side lengths with units directly practises perimeter measurement.
Calculating polygon perimeter is a central perimeter procedure.
Missing-side tasks extend perimeter reasoning to inverse and equation-like contexts.
Composite polygon perimeter extends perimeter to more complex boundaries.
Area as covering is foundational to rectangle and triangle area measurement.
Array models support rectangle area formulas through rows and columns of square units.
Rectangle area formulas are central to this topic.
Square area is a special rectangle-area case.
Triangle area is a core extension from rectangle area.
Parallelogram rearrangement supports later triangle and composite area reasoning.
Decomposing a figure into known shapes is central to composite area.
Recombining part areas directly practises composite area calculation.
Subtracting missing regions is a common composite-area strategy.
Maintaining square units supports accurate composite area work.
Contextual area problems apply composite-area decomposition and calculation.
Radius and diameter are foundational circle measures.
Circumference formula is central to circle boundary measurement.
Circle area formula is central to circle area measurement.
Semicircles and quarter circles extend circle formulas to part-circle figures.
Circle contexts apply circumference and area relationships.
Perimeter as boundary length depends on understanding length units and boundary measurement.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats perimeter as area or counts interior spaces.

edge.rationale: Measuring perimeter with units requires recognising which boundary length is being measured.
edge.failure_signal: Learner measures a side or interior distance rather than the full outside boundary.

edge.rationale: Calculating polygon perimeter builds on measuring and summing side lengths.
edge.failure_signal: Learner omits sides or adds non-boundary dimensions.

edge.rationale: Missing-side perimeter problems require understanding how side lengths sum to a perimeter.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot use the known perimeter and sides to determine an unknown side.

edge.rationale: Composite polygon perimeter extends polygon perimeter to more complex boundaries.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts shared or internal sides as part of the outer perimeter.

edge.rationale: Area as covering builds directly on square-unit area measurement.
edge.failure_signal: Learner describes area with length-only language or linear units.

edge.rationale: Array models for area use row and column structures from multiplication arrays.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts squares one-by-one but cannot use rows and columns to structure area.

edge.rationale: The rectangle area formula generalises the array model of rows and columns of square units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner memorises length times width without understanding square-unit structure.

edge.rationale: Square area is a special case of rectangle area with equal side lengths.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses perimeter-like addition rather than side times side.

edge.rationale: Triangle area is commonly derived as half of a related rectangle or parallelogram.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses base times height without halving for triangles.

edge.rationale: Parallelogram area can be reasoned by rearranging to a rectangle with the same base and height.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses slanted side length as height without considering perpendicular height.

edge.rationale: Composite figure decomposition requires familiarity with areas of simpler component shapes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify known shapes within a composite figure.

edge.rationale: Recombining area parts requires decomposing the figure into measurable pieces first.
edge.failure_signal: Learner decomposes but does not add part areas correctly.

edge.rationale: Subtracting a missing region requires identifying a larger enclosing area and the removed part.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds all visible dimensions rather than subtracting the cut-out region.

edge.rationale: Composite area calculations require consistent use of square units across all parts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner mixes linear and square units or changes units between parts.

edge.rationale: Contextual area problems require selecting and combining appropriate area strategies.
edge.failure_signal: Learner computes part areas but cannot decide which areas answer the context question.

edge.rationale: Circle measurement requires recognising circle features and their parts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify centre, radius or diameter on a circle diagram.

edge.rationale: Circumference formulas use radius or diameter relationships.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses radius and diameter interchangeably in circumference formulas.

edge.rationale: Circle area formula depends on using radius correctly.
edge.failure_signal: Learner substitutes diameter into the radius-squared term.

edge.rationale: Semicircle and quarter-circle problems require applying whole-circle formulas to fractional parts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner calculates a whole circle but forgets to take the appropriate fraction.

edge.rationale: Circle contexts often require distinguishing boundary length from area before calculating.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses the area formula when the context asks for distance around the circle.
